title: Retiring at 36, Sorana Cirstea Just Made History with a 'Double Bagel' at the French Open
summary: Sorana Cirstea is writing a remarkable final chapter to her 20-year career. At 36, the Romanian tennis player has become the oldest competitor in the Open era to deliver a "double bagel"—a 6-0, 6-0 victory—in a Grand Slam main draw. Her flawless win over Argentina's Solana Sierra at the French Open on Friday sent her into the fourth round, making her the oldest woman to reach the last 16 at Roland Garros since Serena Williams in 2021. Cirstea, who announced she will retire at the end of 2026, is enjoying one of the best spells of her career. Earlier this month, she reached the Italian Open semifinals, stunning world number one Aryna Sabalenka along the way. Against the 21-year-old Sierra, Cirstea was utterly dominant. Her opponent never reached game point once in the entire match. "I feel I am still working the same—the same discipline and professionalism," Cirstea said afterward. "Every time I step on court I feel I have a lot of things to improve. I have goals I want to improve and that keeps me alive." She added that consistency has been the key difference this season. For years, Cirstea hovered around the top 20, but deep runs at major tournaments had eluded her. This is the first time she has advanced beyond the second round of a Grand Slam since the 2022 US Open. Now, with a fourth-round match against China's Wang Xiyu, she has a chance to reach the quarterfinals at Roland Garros for the first time in 17 years. That would equal her best-ever Grand Slam result, a quarterfinal appearance at the 2022 US Open. Cirstea's story is a reminder that athletic peaks don't always follow a predictable timeline. While many players her age have long since retired, she is proving that experience and relentless self-improvement can produce extraordinary moments. Her double bagel isn't just a statistical oddity—it's a testament to a veteran athlete refusing to fade quietly.
why_it_matters: Cirstea's late-career success challenges the assumption that elite athletes must peak young. For teenagers navigating pressure to achieve early, her story shows that relentless self-improvement can pay off years later, and that a career can culminate on its own terms.

background_read: A 'double bagel'—two consecutive 6-0 sets—is one of the rarest results in professional tennis, especially at a Grand Slam tournament.
Sorana Cirstea (a Romanian player who turned professional in 2006) beat the world number one, Aryna Sabalenka, just before this historic French Open run.
The French Open, held at Roland Garros in Paris, is played on red clay, a surface that often rewards patience and endurance, traits that serve older players well.

While most top players peak in their mid-20s, Cirstea joins a select group of veterans who have achieved their best results later in their careers, including Serena Williams (who reached Grand Slam finals well into her 30s).
Cirstea's announcement that she will retire at the end of 2026 adds weight to this late-career flourish, making each victory part of a farewell tour.

perspectives.description: For Cirstea, this double bagel is a crowning achievement in a twilight career, proving that veteran athletes can still dominate. Her win inspires older players and fans who appreciate perseverance over youthful flash.

Critics might note that such a lopsided result at a Grand Slam raises concerns about depth in women's tennis; a 21-year-old failing to win a single game may reflect a gap in the younger generation's readiness.

Statistically, double bagels are so rare that each one invites analysis of playing conditions and mental toughness. Cirstea's aggressive baseline game and clay-court patience illustrate how experience can dismantle a less seasoned opponent.

If Cirstea advances further, it could reshape conversations about retirement age in tennis, encouraging more players to extend their careers. Her farewell tour may also prompt the WTA to create more legacy honor for veterans.
